newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM palladium seen supported by short overhang.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM palladium seen supported by short overhang.

text.p: A large overhang of short positions in Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) palladium futures is likely to prevent the market falling sharply after Russia resumes exports of the metal, traders said on Wednesday.

Short positions held by private investors had fallen to the equivalent of around 46 tonnes as of Tuesday from around 60 tonnes at the end of May, but the volume remains massive compared with normal levels, traders said.
In 1996, global palladium supplies totalled about 186 tonnes.

Private investors have been avidly building short positions in palladium futures since the start of this year, believing the suspension of Russian sales will be short-lived and that prices will fall once Russia resumes exports.

"The key is whether palladium prices will dip significantly after the resumption of Russian sales. If prices do not slip private investors are expected to cover their shorts," one analyst at a commodity broker said.

The Russian platinum group metal (PGM) export agency (Almazjuvelirexport) has told Japanese clients it will resume sales in the spot market in late June, and that deliveries under long-term contracts will resume in July.
Palladium futures prices have been surprisingly resilient and maintained high levels, despite news that Almaz plans to resume sales.
In afternoon trade on Wednesday, benchmark palladium was quoted at 562 yen per gram, compared to around 445 yen at the beginning of this year.
Traders say private investors have already lost a lot of money and are desperate to cover their short positions.
"Private investors who built short positions at lower prices, especially in the August, October and December futures contracts are suffering heavy losses and margin calls," one trader said.
"Any price dip could provide an opportunity to cover short positions. Palladium prices could be supported until the TOCOM December palladium expires later this year (in December)," the trader said.
